definition: a person who has committed a crime
example: First-time offenders are often given community sentences instead of prison terms.

definition: a person who carries out a harmful or illegal act
example: Police have not yet identified the perpetrator of the attack on the bank.

definition: the crime of entering a building illegally in order to steal
example: Burglary fell by a fifth after residents installed better locks and security lighting.

definition: the crime of stealing from a person or place using force or threats
example: The armed robbery lasted less than two minutes, but the cashier was left deeply shaken.

definition: the crime of taking goods from a shop without paying
example: Shoplifting costs retailers millions of pounds a year and raises prices for honest customers.

definition: the deliberate damage of public or private property
example: Bright lighting and cameras in the car park have reduced vandalism considerably.

definition: the crime of deceiving someone in order to gain money or an advantage illegally
example: The accountant was jailed for fraud after altering the company's records for several years.

definition: the crime of secretly taking money that has been placed in your care
example: The treasurer was accused of embezzlement after thousands of pounds disappeared from the charity.

definition: the offering of money or gifts to persuade someone to act dishonestly
example: Bribery in the construction industry can result in poorly built and unsafe buildings.

definition: the crime of deliberately setting fire to a building
example: Fire investigators believe the warehouse blaze was a case of arson rather than an accident.

definition: a violent physical attack on a person
example: He was charged with assault after a fight outside a nightclub left another man in hospital.

definition: the killing of one person by another
example: The homicide rate in the region has fallen steadily over the past decade.

definition: the illegal trade in people, drugs or weapons
example: International cooperation is essential to combat human trafficking across borders.

definition: the illegal movement of goods or people into or out of a country
example: Customs officers uncovered a smuggling operation hidden inside a shipment of furniture.

definition: made as a copy of something valuable in order to deceive people
example: Counterfeit medicines are dangerous because they may contain the wrong ingredients.

definition: the crime of making a false copy of a document, signature or work of art
example: Experts concluded that the signature on the will was a forgery.

definition: minor crime or antisocial behaviour, especially by young people
example: Poverty and a lack of supervision are often cited as causes of delinquency among teenagers.

definition: a young person who has broken the law
example: Many experts believe a juvenile offender should receive education rather than a prison sentence.

definition: to commit another crime after having been punished for an earlier one
example: Prisoners who learn a trade during their sentence are less likely to reoffend after release.

definition: the tendency of a convicted criminal to commit further crimes
example: Rehabilitation programmes aim to lower recidivism by helping prisoners find jobs.

definition: the process of helping an offender return to normal life in society
example: Supporters of rehabilitation argue that prison should prepare inmates for life outside.

definition: something that discourages people from doing an action by making them afraid of the result
example: Visible police patrols are a powerful deterrent to street crime.

definition: the punishment given to a person found guilty in a court
example: The judge handed down a two-year sentence, which was later reduced on appeal.

definition: the state of being kept in prison as a punishment
example: Imprisonment removes dangerous people from society, but it does little to change their behaviour.

definition: unpaid work done for the benefit of the public instead of a prison term
example: Teenagers who damaged the bus shelter were ordered to complete eighty hours of community service.

definition: a period during which an offender is supervised in the community instead of being in prison
example: He was placed on probation for two years and had to report to an officer every week.

definition: the early release of a prisoner on condition of good behaviour
example: She was released on parole after serving half of her sentence.

definition: to prove or declare in a court that someone is guilty of a crime
example: A suspect can only be convicted if the jury believes the evidence beyond reasonable doubt.

definition: to decide in a court that a person is not guilty of a crime
example: The jury acquitted the defendant after a witness admitted she had lied.

definition: to take legal action against someone accused of a crime
example: Shops rarely prosecute children for stealing small items and usually contact their parents instead.

definition: to give evidence as a witness in a court of law
example: Two neighbours agreed to testify against the man accused of the break-in.

definition: a person who sees a crime or an accident and can describe what happened
example: A key witness came forward after the police published a photograph of the car.

definition: facts or signs that help prove whether something is true or a person is guilty
example: There was not enough evidence to charge the man, so he was released the following morning.

definition: a person who is thought to have committed a crime
example: The prime suspect was seen on camera leaving the shop shortly before the alarm sounded.

definition: to take a person into custody because they are thought to have committed a crime
example: Officers arrested two men outside the jeweller's shop late on Friday night.

definition: to keep someone in official custody or prevent them from leaving
example: Under the new law, police may detain a suspect for up to twenty-four hours without charge.

definition: to question a person closely, often for a long time
example: Detectives interrogate suspects in a room where all conversations are recorded.

definition: to catch and arrest a person suspected of a crime
example: Police managed to apprehend the thief within minutes of the alarm being raised.

definition: a formal examination of a legal case in a court
example: The trial lasted three weeks, and the court heard from more than twenty witnesses.

definition: the official decision of a jury or judge about whether a person is guilty
example: The jury took only two hours to reach a unanimous verdict.

definition: a group of ordinary citizens who decide whether a person is guilty in a court
example: Serving on a jury is a civic duty that many people find both interesting and stressful.

definition: a person who is accused of a crime in a court of law
example: The defendant pleaded not guilty and insisted that he had been at home all evening.

definition: always obeying the law and its rules
example: Most law-abiding citizens would never dream of stealing, even if they could avoid being caught.

definition: minor illegal acts such as small thefts
example: Petty crime such as pickpocketing is common in crowded tourist areas.

definition: illegal activity carried out by well-structured criminal groups
example: Organised crime depends on corruption, and it often operates across several countries at once.

definition: a crime in which people are harmed or threatened with harm
example: Violent crime is more frequent in areas where unemployment and poverty are high.

definition: illegal activity carried out using computers or the internet
example: Cybercrime is growing quickly because criminals can target victims anywhere in the world.

definition: the crime of using another person's personal details to obtain money or goods
example: Never share your passwords, because identity theft can take years to resolve.

definition: the close observation of people or places in order to prevent or detect crime
example: Increased surveillance in public places has raised concerns about personal privacy.

definition: a regular journey around an area by police to prevent crime
example: More foot patrols in the town centre have made shoppers feel safer at night.

definition: severe action taken by authorities to stop an illegal activity
example: The government announced a crackdown on illegal gambling after several complaints.

definition: the legal killing of a person as a punishment for a serious crime
example: Opponents of capital punishment argue that it can never be undone if a mistake is made.

definition: a punishment under which a criminal stays in prison for the rest of their life or a very long time
example: A life sentence for murder is the norm in many legal systems.

definition: not as strict as expected when punishing someone
example: Many people feel that courts are too lenient with repeat offenders.

definition: intended as punishment, especially a severe one
example: A purely punitive approach to crime seldom reduces the likelihood of reoffending.

definition: severe punishment given as a payment for a wrong that has been done
example: Some victims' families regard a long prison term as retribution rather than justice.

definition: a deep feeling of guilt about something wrong that you have done
example: The judge reduced the sentence because the young man showed genuine remorse.

definition: the person who is responsible for a crime or something bad
example: Security footage helped detectives to identify the culprit within a day.

definition: a person who helps someone else to commit a crime
example: The robber and his accomplice were both arrested at the airport.

definition: a thief who steals from people's pockets or bags in crowded places
example: Tourists are warned to watch for a pickpocket on busy trains and in markets.

definition: to steal goods from shops or homes during a riot or disaster
example: Crowds began to loot shops after the power cut that followed the storm.

definition: money demanded in exchange for the release of a kidnapped person
example: The family paid a large ransom but their daughter was not released for another week.

definition: to take someone away illegally and hold them, often to demand money
example: Armed men attempted to kidnap the businessman as he left his office.

definition: the crime of threatening to reveal secrets unless money is paid
example: The official resigned after admitting that he had been a victim of blackmail.

definition: the crime of obtaining money by using force or threats
example: Shopkeepers in the district have been paying extortion money to local gangs for years.

definition: the process of making illegally obtained money appear to come from a legal source
example: Banks must report suspicious transfers to help prevent money laundering.

definition: a group of criminals or young people who spend time together and cause trouble
example: Teenagers sometimes join a gang because they want protection or a sense of belonging.

definition: famous for something bad
example: The district was notorious for pickpockets, and few tourists dared to visit at night.

definition: a minor offence that is not considered very serious
example: Dropping litter is a misdemeanour that is punishable by a small fine.

definition: the number of crimes committed in an area compared with its population
example: The crime rate dropped sharply after the council introduced late-night buses and brighter streets.

definition: the activity of making sure that people obey the law
example: Effective law enforcement requires trust between the police and the community.

definition: using scientific methods to investigate crime
example: Forensic evidence, such as fingerprints and DNA, linked the suspect to the scene.

definition: proof that a person was somewhere else when a crime took place
example: He had a solid alibi, because he was in a meeting with six colleagues at the time.

definition: a formal decision in a court that someone is guilty of a crime
example: A criminal conviction can make it very hard for a person to find work.

definition: actions that harm or annoy other people in a community
example: Loud music and graffiti are common examples of antisocial behaviour in residential areas.

definition: measures taken to stop crime before it happens
example: Community crime prevention schemes often work better than harsher punishments.

definition: a scheme in which residents look out for crime in their own area
example: Our neighbourhood watch group shares information about suspicious activity by text message.

definition: relating to the punishment of criminals
example: Penal reform advocates argue that prison should be a last resort rather than the default punishment.

definition: a situation in which prisons hold more inmates than they were designed for
example: Prison overcrowding makes it difficult to offer education programmes that help inmates to change.

definition: the illegal copying and selling of films, music, software or other protected work
example: Streaming services have reduced online piracy by making legal content cheaper and easier to access.

definition: crime or antisocial behaviour committed by young people
example: Researchers have linked juvenile delinquency to truancy and a lack of supervision after school.
